rationale: A wins because it keeps the causal gun unloaded: "Flat prices, rising food costs, undisclosed labor savings: the math behind Chipotle's freeze" invites skepticism without claiming Chipotle proved the math. B repeatedly fires before it aims: "Its Avocado Robot Explains Why" and "Chipotle Says Its Robots Justify Flat Prices" assert the causal link the update never gives. Same raw material, but A teaches the founder where the story is and where the hole starts.
gaps_in_A: "The reporter can do the arithmetic from the supplied facts alone" overstates what the supplied facts can prove; 100 of 3,500 stores is suggestive, not a full margin model.
"The prevailing belief is that chains pass food-cost inflation straight to the menu" is a useful setup, but it needs market context if this becomes the lead angle.
gaps_in_B: "Its Avocado Robot Explains Why" invents the central causal link. The update says the robot rollout and price hold coexist; it does not say one explains the other.
"Chipotle Says Its Robots Justify Flat Prices" is flatly overclaimed. Chipotle did not say that in the supplied facts.
"Its Competitors Are Taking Notes" invents competitor reaction. No rival, analyst, or operator evidence was supplied.
"Labor Advocates Are Watching" may be a smart reporting move, but the headline asserts outside scrutiny the update does not show.
